title: 2.5 · Part II
note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can find the range and the interquartile range of a data set and use them to describe how spread out the data is.
languageObjective: I can explain what the spread of a data set is using the words range, quartile, interquartile range, and vary.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers that describe spread: the range covers all the data, and the interquartile range covers only the middle half.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números que describen la dispersión: el rango cubre todos los datos y el rango intercuartílico solo la mitad central.
vocabulary.visual: Range 26 covers 68 to 94; IQR 12.5 covers only 75.5 to 88
vocabulary.cloze: The range uses the ___ values; the interquartile range uses the ___.

examples.why: The IQR is always the smaller of the two — it sits inside the range.
The middle half cannot be wider than all of the data.

vocabulary.definition: The distance from the least value to the greatest value, found by subtracting: greatest − least.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia del valor menor al mayor, que se halla restando: mayor − menor.
vocabulary.cloze: Subtract the least value from the ___ value to find the range.

examples.why: A range is a difference, never a sum.

vocabulary.definition: One of the three values that cut an ordered data set into four equal-sized groups.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Uno de los tres valores que dividen un conjunto ordenado de datos en cuatro grupos del mismo tamaño.

examples.why: It is the median OF that half.
That is the minimum, not a quartile.

vocabulary.cloze: Numbers that split ordered data into four equal parts are ___.

vocabulary.definition: The distance across the middle half of the data, found by subtracting the first quartile from the third: Q3 − Q1.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia a lo largo de la mitad central de los datos: se resta el primer cuartil del tercero: Q3 − Q1.
vocabulary.visual: 88 − 75.5 = 12.5 — the width of the box on a box plot

examples.why: Q3 minus Q1 — the middle half's width.
That is the range, using the extremes.

vocabulary.cloze: The spread of the middle half of the data, Q3 − Q1, is the ___ ___.

vocabulary.definition: How much the values in a data set differ from one another — whether they sit close together or far apart.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto se diferencian entre sí los valores de un conjunto de datos: si están juntos o muy separados.
vocabulary.visual: Close together = low variability; spread apart = high variability

examples.why: The values differ, which is what variability measures.
Nothing varies, so there is no spread to describe.

vocabulary.cloze: How spread out the numbers in a data set are is its ___.

vocabulary.definition: A single number that describes the spread of a whole data set. The range and the IQR are both measures of variation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número que describe la dispersión de todo un conjunto de datos. El rango y el RIC son medidas de variación.
vocabulary.visual: One number stands in for the spread of all 20 scores
vocabulary.cloze: A single number describing how spread out a data set is is a ___ ___ ___.

examples.why: It reports spread in one number.
That reports the center, not the spread.

vocabulary.definition: The least or greatest value in a data set, far from the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El valor menor o mayor de un conjunto de datos, lejos del resto.
vocabulary.visual: An extreme value stretches the range.
vocabulary.cloze: The least or greatest value, far from the others, is an ___.

examples.text: A score of 68 when the other scores are between 82 and 94
examples.why: It sits far below the rest of the data.

examples.text: A score of 86 when the other scores are between 82 and 94
examples.why: It sits in the middle of the data.

items.meaning: The distance from the least value to the greatest value

copyPanel.formula: Range = Maximum − Minimum | IQR = Q3 − Q1
steps: 1. Range measures the total spread across the entire data set
2. IQR (Interquartile Range) measures the spread of the middle 50% of data
3. Both are non-negative distance measures of variability

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Professional Basketball
revealWordProblem.text:
The two box plots show the salaries, in millions of dollars, for 15 players on two different professional basketball teams.
Question: A basketball player hopes to be drafted by a professional basketball team. Should he hope to be drafted by Team A or Team B? Use the range and the interquartile range in your answer.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two box plots of player salaries in millions of dollars, one for Team A and one for Team B, drawn on the same number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Read the approximate values from the shared salary axis. Team A runs from about $1 million to $20 million, so its range is about $19 million. Team B runs from about $1 million to $40 million, so its range is about $39 million. Team A's box runs from about $2 million to $10.5 million, giving an IQR near $8.5 million. Team B's box runs from a little over $2 million to about $9 million, giving an IQR near $7 million. Team B has the larger overall range but the slightly smaller IQR: its middle half is not more spread out. A player seeking the highest observed salary might prefer Team B, but the plots cannot predict a new player's salary. Either recommendation needs a reason tied to the range and the IQR, rather than treating the maximum as a typical salary.

questions.stem: A data set runs from a least value of 12 to a greatest value of 30. What is the range?
choiceFeedback: 12 is the least value, not the distance between the two ends.
21 is halfway between 12 and 30 — that is a center, not a spread.
30 is the greatest value, not the distance between the two ends.
hints: Range asks how far it is from one end of the data to the other.
Find the greatest value and the least value, then subtract.
questions.stemEs: Un conjunto de datos va de un valor menor de 12 a un valor mayor de 30. ¿Cuál es el rango?
hintsEs: El rango pregunta qué tan lejos está un extremo de los datos del otro.
Halla el valor mayor y el valor menor, y luego resta.

questions.stem: On a box plot, Q1 = 20 and Q3 = 36. What is the interquartile range?
choiceFeedback: 28 is halfway between 20 and 36 — that is a middle, not a width.
36 is Q3 by itself, not the distance from Q1 to Q3.
That is 36 + 20. The IQR is a difference, so subtract.
hints: The IQR is the width of the box on a box plot.
The box runs from Q1 to Q3, so subtract Q1 from Q3.
questions.stemEs: En un diagrama de caja, Q1 = 20 y Q3 = 36. ¿Cuál es el rango intercuartílico?
hintsEs: El RIC es el ancho de la caja en un diagrama de caja.
La caja va de Q1 a Q3, así que resta Q1 de Q3.

questions.stem: Which measure of spread uses ONLY the middle half of the data?
questions.explanation: The IQR runs from Q1 to Q3, which is exactly the middle half of the values. The range is the distance from the minimum to the maximum; interior values do not enter that subtraction.
choiceFeedback: The range stretches from the least value to the greatest; it is calculated from those two extremes.
The median is a measure of center, not of spread.
The mode is the most common value — also not a measure of spread.
hints: One is measured across the box on a box plot; the other whisker to whisker.
The box holds the middle 50% of the data.
Q1 to Q3 is the middle half.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál medida de dispersión usa SOLO la mitad central de los datos?
questions.explanationEs: El RIC va de Q1 a Q3 y describe la mitad central de los datos. El rango es la distancia entre el mínimo y el máximo; los valores interiores no entran en esa resta.
hintsEs: Uno se mide a lo ancho de la caja en un diagrama de caja; el otro de bigote a bigote.
La caja contiene el 50% central de los datos.
De Q1 a Q3 es la mitad central.

reviewHighlights.formula: Range = Maximum − Minimum | IQR = Q3 − Q1
steps: 1. Range measures the total spread across the entire data set
2. IQR (Interquartile Range) measures the spread of the middle 50% of data
3. Both are non-negative distance measures of variability
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake with Range and Interquartile Range is adding the two quartiles instead of subtracting them — writing IQR = Q3 + Q1. With Q1 = 42 and Q3 = 58 that gives 100, which is larger than the data set's entire range of 20. Every measure of variation is a DIFFERENCE, and the IQR can never exceed the range, because the middle half is part of the whole span. If your IQR comes out bigger than your range, you added when you should have subtracted.

level1.stem: A box plot shows: least 3, Q1 7, median 10, Q3 14, greatest 18. What is the range?
level1.stemEs: Un diagrama de caja muestra: menor 3, Q1 7, mediana 10, Q3 14, mayor 18. ¿Cuál es el rango?
hints: The range uses the least and greatest values.
hintsEs: El rango usa el valor menor y el mayor.
level1.explanation: Find the least and greatest values: 3 and 18 Subtract the least from the greatest: 18 − 3 = 15
level1.explanationEs: Busca el valor menor y el mayor: 3 y 18 Resta el menor del mayor: 18 − 3 = 15

level1.stem: A box plot shows: least 20, Q1 24, median 29, Q3 33, greatest 41. What is the IQR?
level1.stemEs: Un diagrama de caja muestra: menor 20, Q1 24, mediana 29, Q3 33, mayor 41. ¿Cuál es el RIC?
hints: The IQR uses Q1 and Q3.
hintsEs: El RIC usa Q1 y Q3.
level1.explanation: Find Q1 and Q3: Q1 = 24, Q3 = 33 Subtract Q1 from Q3: 33 − 24 = 9
level1.explanationEs: Busca Q1 y Q3: Q1 = 24, Q3 = 33 Resta Q1 de Q3: 33 − 24 = 9

hints: Find the least and greatest values first.
hintsEs: Primero busca el valor menor y el mayor.
level1.explanation: Find the least and greatest values: 8 and 22 Subtract the least from the greatest: 22 − 8 = 14
level1.explanationEs: Busca el valor menor y el mayor: 8 y 22 Resta el menor del mayor: 22 − 8 = 14

level1.stem: A box plot shows: least 2, Q1 4, median 6, Q3 9, greatest 12. What is the IQR?
level1.stemEs: Un diagrama de caja muestra: menor 2, Q1 4, mediana 6, Q3 9, mayor 12. ¿Cuál es el RIC?
hints: The IQR uses Q1 and Q3 only.
hintsEs: El RIC usa solo Q1 y Q3.
level1.explanation: Find Q1 and Q3: Q1 = 4, Q3 = 9 Subtract Q1 from Q3: 9 − 4 = 5
level1.explanationEs: Busca Q1 y Q3: Q1 = 4, Q3 = 9 Resta Q1 de Q3: 9 − 4 = 5

level1.stem: Find the range of these test scores: 72, 88, 61, 93, 78, 81, 69.
level1.stemEs: Halla el rango de estas calificaciones: 72, 88, 61, 93, 78, 81, 69.
hints: Find the least and the greatest score first. They are not at the ends of the list.
hintsEs: Primero busca la calificación menor y la mayor. No están en los extremos de la lista.
level1.explanation: Find the least and greatest scores: 61 and 93 Subtract the least from the greatest: 93 − 61 = 32
level1.explanationEs: Busca la calificación menor y la mayor: 61 y 93 Resta la menor de la mayor: 93 − 61 = 32

level2.stem: Class D has a range of 30 and an IQR of 8. Class E has a range of 22 and an IQR of 15. Which class has its middle half of scores closer together?
level2.stemEs: La clase D tiene un rango de 30 y un RIC de 8. La clase E tiene un rango de 22 y un RIC de 15. ¿Qué clase tiene la mitad central de sus calificaciones más junta?
hints: Which measure tells about the middle half of the data?
hintsEs: ¿Qué medida habla de la mitad central de los datos?
level2.explanation: Choose the measure for the middle half: the IQR Compare the two IQRs: 8 < 15
level2.explanationEs: Elige la medida de la mitad central: el RIC Compara los dos RIC: 8 < 15
choiceFeedback: Class E has the smaller range, but the question asks about the middle half. That is the IQR.
The IQRs are 8 and 15. They are not the same.

hints: There are 8 values, so each half has 4. Q1 and Q3 are each between two values.
hintsEs: Hay 8 valores, así que cada mitad tiene 4. Q1 y Q3 están cada uno entre dos valores.
level2.explanation: Find Q1 from the lower half: (3 + 4.5) ÷ 2 = 3.75 Find Q3 from the upper half: (7.5 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.75 Subtract Q1 from Q3: 7.75 − 3.75 = 4
level2.explanationEs: Halla Q1 con la mitad inferior: (3 + 4.5) ÷ 2 = 3.75 Halla Q3 con la mitad superior: (7.5 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.75 Resta Q1 de Q3: 7.75 − 3.75 = 4

level2.stem: A box plot shows: least 10, Q1 16, median 21, Q3 27, greatest 35. What is the IQR?
level2.stemEs: Un diagrama de caja muestra: menor 10, Q1 16, mediana 21, Q3 27, mayor 35. ¿Cuál es el RIC?
hints: Subtract Q1 from Q3.
hintsEs: Resta Q1 de Q3.
level2.explanation: Find Q1 and Q3: Q1 = 16, Q3 = 27 Subtract Q1 from Q3: 27 − 16 = 11
level2.explanationEs: Busca Q1 y Q3: Q1 = 16, Q3 = 27 Resta Q1 de Q3: 27 − 16 = 11

level2.stem: A box plot has Q3 = 48 and an IQR of 17. What is Q1?
level2.stemEs: Un diagrama de caja tiene Q3 = 48 y un RIC de 17. ¿Cuánto es Q1?
hints: IQR = Q3 − Q1. Work backward from Q3.
hintsEs: RIC = Q3 − Q1. Trabaja hacia atrás desde Q3.
level2.explanation: Write the IQR equation: 48 − Q1 = 17 Work backward: 48 − 17 = 31
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la ecuación del RIC: 48 − Q1 = 17 Trabaja hacia atrás: 48 − 17 = 31

level2.stem: The high temperatures for 9 days were 58, 61, 62, 65, 66, 68, 70, 71 and 77 °F. What is the range?
level2.stemEs: Las temperaturas máximas de 9 días fueron 58, 61, 62, 65, 66, 68, 70, 71 y 77 °F. ¿Cuál es el rango?
hints: The range uses only the least and greatest values.
hintsEs: El rango usa solo el valor menor y el mayor.
level2.explanation: Find the least and greatest temperatures: 58 and 77 Subtract the least from the greatest: 77 − 58 = 19
level2.explanationEs: Busca la temperatura menor y la mayor: 58 y 77 Resta la menor de la mayor: 77 − 58 = 19

level3.stem: Two classes have the same median score of 81. Class A scores range from 78 to 84; Class B scores range from 60 to 99. What does this tell you?
choices: Class B has a higher median.
Class B has greater variability, even though the centers are the same.
choiceFeedback: Both medians are 81, as the question states. What differs between the classes is how spread out the scores are.
Neither range tells you how many students there are. A range describes spread, not count.
The centers match, but Class A spans 6 points and Class B spans 39.
level3.explanation: Class A's range is 84 − 78 = 6; Class B's is 99 − 60 = 39. Equal centers can hide very different spreads, which is what measures of variability reveal.

level3.stem: Data: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. A new value, 50, is added. Which measure changes more?
level3.stemEs: Datos: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Se agrega un valor nuevo, 50. ¿Qué medida cambia más?
hints: Find the range and the IQR before and after you add 50.
hintsEs: Halla el rango y el RIC antes y después de agregar 50.
level3.explanation: Find the range before and after: 15 − 10 = 5; 50 − 10 = 40 Find the IQR before and after: 14 − 11 = 3; 15 − 11 = 4
level3.explanationEs: Halla el rango antes y después: 15 − 10 = 5; 50 − 10 = 40 Halla el RIC antes y después: 14 − 11 = 3; 15 − 11 = 4
choices: They change by the same amount.
choiceFeedback: The IQR only goes from 3 to 4. The middle half barely moves.
The range grows by 35. The IQR grows by only 1.

hints: Each half has 4 values. The value 45 is in the upper half, but it is not a middle value.
hintsEs: Cada mitad tiene 4 valores. El 45 está en la mitad superior, pero no es un valor del medio.
level3.explanation: Find Q1 from the lower half: (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5 Find Q3 from the upper half: (20 + 21) ÷ 2 = 20.5 Subtract Q1 from Q3: 20.5 − 14.5 = 6
level3.explanationEs: Halla Q1 con la mitad inferior: (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5 Halla Q3 con la mitad superior: (20 + 21) ÷ 2 = 20.5 Resta Q1 de Q3: 20.5 − 14.5 = 6

level3.stem: Nina ran a race 7 times. Her times in seconds were 31, 33, 34, 35, 36, 38 and 52. Which measure best describes how spread out most of her times are?
level3.stemEs: Nina corrió una carrera 7 veces. Sus tiempos en segundos fueron 31, 33, 34, 35, 36, 38 y 52. ¿Qué medida describe mejor qué tan dispersos están la mayoría de sus tiempos?
hints: One time is far from the rest. Which measure does it not stretch?
hintsEs: Un tiempo está lejos de los demás. ¿Qué medida no se estira por él?
choiceFeedback: The range is 21, but the slow time of 52 stretches it. Most times are close together.
21 is the range, 52 − 31. The IQR is 38 − 33 = 5.
5 is the IQR, not the range. The range is 52 − 31 = 21.

level3.stem: Eight values in order are 3, ?, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20. The IQR is 10. Find the missing value.
level3.stemEs: Ocho valores en orden son 3, ?, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20. El RIC es 10. Halla el valor que falta.
hints: Find Q3 first. Then use the IQR to find Q1.
hintsEs: Primero halla Q3. Luego usa el RIC para hallar Q1.
level3.explanation: Find Q3 from the upper half: (15 + 17) ÷ 2 = 16 Use the IQR to find Q1: 16 − 10 = 6 Work backward to the missing value: (? + 8) ÷ 2 = 6; 6 × 2 = 12; 12 − 8 = 4
level3.explanationEs: Halla Q3 con la mitad superior: (15 + 17) ÷ 2 = 16 Usa el RIC para hallar Q1: 16 − 10 = 6 Trabaja hacia atrás hasta el valor que falta: (? + 8) ÷ 2 = 6; 6 × 2 = 12; 12 − 8 = 4
